title: Squared error and level-one Fourier weight
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, viewed as a real-valued function. Write $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb{E}_x[f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i]$ for its Fourier coefficient at a coordinate set $S$, and let $f_1(x)=\sum_{|S|=1}\widehat f(S)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ be its degree-one part. Then $\mathbb{E}_x[(f(x)-f_1(x))^2]=1-\sum_{|S|=1}\widehat f(S)^2$, where the expectations are uniform on the sign cube.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
